claims.text: 3D ink extrusion printing, hydrogen de-binding, vacuum sintering at 1400 °C for 18 hours, and use of a titanium sponge oxygen getter improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The starting ink contains HfH2, NbH, TaH0.5, TiH2, ZrH2, metallic Ti/Nb, and a polystyrene/binder matrix.
Effective processing requires a vacuum below 3×10^-6 torr.
The material is vacuum-sintered at 1400 °C for 18 hours.
Water quenching from approximately 1500 °C suppresses undesired alpha-HCP formation.
The proposed oxygen-resistance boundary is exposure to air at 800 °C for up to 5 hours.
The hydrides decompose sequentially in the order Ta, Nb, then Hf/Ti/Zr because of their differing formation enthalpies.
Sequential hydride decomposition enables in-situ alloying and oxygen scavenging.
The process forms a thin silicide coating.
The silicide coating transforms into a self-healing (Zr,Hf)O2 layer during high-temperature exposure.
Processing produces controlled oxygen uptake of approximately 1.0 wt.%.
Approximately 1.0 wt.% oxygen uptake causes interstitial strengthening.
Controlled oxygen uptake and quenching stabilize a metastable beta-BCC structure.
The silicide-derived oxide layer acts as an oxidation barrier and reduces oxygen ingress relative to untreated cast material.
The processed material will be almost fully dense.
The processed material will exhibit a nearly single metastable beta-BCC phase.
The intervention will preserve room-temperature tensile ductility and high-temperature yield strength.
The intervention will significantly reduce the oxidation rate relative to cast HfNbTaTiZr or uncoated sintered samples.
Untreated cast or uncoated sintered material has an oxidation constant of approximately 570 mg² cm^-4 h^-1 under similar exposure conditions.
Untreated material undergoes rapid oxidation, cracking, and embrittlement associated with alpha-HCP formation.

contradictions.description: A silicide coating is invoked as a central mediator, but neither the stated ink formulation nor the intervention contains a silicon-bearing precursor or coating step.
The thermal profile specifies sintering or sequential heating only to 1400 °C but then specifies quenching from approximately 1500 °C, without defining an intervening heating step to 1500 °C.

The requested target and principal baseline are cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr, whereas the intervention is formulated as manufacture of a new powder-derived printed and sintered material rather than treatment of the stated cast material.
